_meta.interpretation: Each row splits one region's customers into those who converted and those who did not, so the two cells of a row sum to one and the yes cell is that region's conversion rate. Most regions convert a little over a third of their customers; north converts noticeably more. With around a hundred customers per region a gap that size can easily arise by chance: shares describe the mix, they do not test it, so run a chi-square test across the regions before calling north different. The row margin keeps each region's raw count beside its shares.
_meta.question: What share of customers in each region converted?
_meta.description: Region × converted count crosstab with row normalization. Cells in each row sum to 1, so the value at (region, converted=yes) is the conversion rate within that region.
_meta.name: crosstab_row_normalize_conversion_rate
